<a id="stagecraft"></a>

## Curator scope

Topic `stagecraft`.

If TunnelVision also manages a required, curator or lore-select book, author Setup shows a dismissable degradation. It lists books whose normal keyword scanning TunnelVision suppresses and books it can write. Keyword-trigger passthrough or native injection removes the scan risk. Read-only permission removes the write risk only when its lifecycle, post-turn and sidecar writers are off: the researched version's background writers do not all enforce that permission. Disable TunnelVision for these books to keep those writers out. Both risks must be absent for the warning to clear. Story Orchestrator's protected-span markers constrain its own curator only, not another extension's writers. The check reads settings without changing them and is quiet when TunnelVision is off or the story uses different books.

Fields: `stagecraft.lorebooks`, `stagecraft.exclude`, `stagecraft.createCap` (`schema.ts` `StoryStagecraft`, `StagecraftExclusion`, `stagecraft/scope.ts`, `stagecraft/createPlan.ts`).

- **What it does.** The only lorebooks the World Info curator may edit, for this story: it keeps the story's own lore current as play goes. Its proposals are reviewed and applied at a boundary. Nothing is inferred from requirements; an empty list means no curator writes. `stagecraft.exclude` (`[{ "lorebook": "...", "comments": ["..."] }]`) names entries inside those books that the curator is never shown and may never write (`isCuratorWritable` refuses them at the write edge too); match is by entry title (comment), ignoring case. Inside an entry's content, `{{// so:protect}}` … `{{// so:end}}` marks words the curator may never change: a rewrite that drops them, a patch that crosses them or switching the entry off is refused, when proposed and again when written (an unclosed `so:protect` protects to the end). `{{// so:auto}}` anywhere in a non-constant entry lets the curator's changes to it apply on their own when its changes are set to apply on their own; every other entry still waits for you. Constant (always-on) entries always wait for review, even with `so:auto`; you may still approve them explicitly. SillyTavern drops these `{{// …}}` markers before the prompt, so they cost nothing (`stagecraft/curatorTiers.ts`). The curator may also propose a **new** keyed entry: only in these books, only for a person, place, group or thing that at least two live memory facts name by its title or first key, never for a cast member or with a cast name as a key, never beside an excluded or beat-gated title, never carrying a `{{// …}}` marker. Each new entry waits for the author whatever the accept mode, is written at the next boundary, and a rollback past it deletes it unless it was edited since. `stagecraft.createCap` (0 to 20, default 5) caps new entries per chat; 0 switches creation off for the story. A new-entry card names any existing entry that reads as the same thing (by meaning through SillyTavern's vectors when the install has them, otherwise by wording) and suggests patching that entry instead (`stagecraft/createNearDup.ts`). A written new entry ends with `{{// so:created <chat> | <group>}}`, dropped before the prompt like the other markers; the curator may never add, move or forge one, and a rewrite keeps it. A stamped entry is scanned only in the chat its stamp names: another chat, a fresh run of the same story in the same group included, never sees it, whichever way the book is loaded (`runtime/storyLore.ts` `withoutForeignCreated`). When that chat is deleted you are asked whether to delete the entries it created; an entry without that chat's stamp is never offered, and nothing is deleted without your yes (`runtime/createdReaper.ts`). Leave the stamp in place: an entry without it stays in the book for good. A curator book of 40 entries or more is read as a digest, with no setting: the entries that best match where the story is, what has happened and its open threads (at most 16) are shown in full, and every other entry only by title, grouped by initial (at most 300 titles; any beyond are not listed and cannot be touched). The curator may still switch a title-only entry on or off, but a rewrite or patch of an entry it saw only by title is refused when proposed and again when written, so nothing is edited unseen; an edit moved at review onto another entry than the one it was proposed for is refused when written. Protected spans, constant-entry review, exclusions and gated entries apply to every entry, shown or not; a smaller book is shown in full as before. The new-entry pass still sees every entry in full (`stagecraft/digest.ts`).
- **Good.** `{ "lorebooks": ["Sunken Ruins Chronicle"] }`, a book seeded with the story-state entries play will change; `"exclude": [{ "lorebook": "Story Lore", "comments": ["House style"] }]` for a meta entry that sets the book's voice.
- **Bad.** A curator book that beat lore also gates; a style or rules entry left open to curator rewrites; expecting "apply on their own" to write an entry with no `{{// so:auto}}`.
- **If wrong.** A book with no entries gets only new-entry cards, and only for what two facts establish; seed it with the entries play should keep current. It is never shown and never writes an entry any beat's `world_info` names, because the path replay would undo the write; a gated curator book silently disables the feature.

<a id="lore-select"></a>

## Lore select

Topic `lore-select`.

Fields: `lore_select.lorebooks`, `top_k` (1 to 12), `min_p` (0 to 1), `exclusive`, `position` (`"authored"` or `"depth"`) (`schema.ts` `StoryLoreSelect`, `validate/storyOptions.ts` `readLoreSelect`).

- **What it does.** The judge picks the entries of these books that matter for the next reply and forces them in, even without their keywords. `top_k` caps the picks; `min_p` is the confidence a pick needs. The judge is not asked about an entry SillyTavern's own keyword scan is certain to switch on for that reply, nor about an entry keyed by the drafted member's own name or alias; those are left to the scan. `exclusive: true` also switches off, for that one reply, the entries of these books it did not pick (only with per-chat gating, the default, and never for constant, gated or timed entries, or an entry left to the scan). `position: "authored"` keeps this story's per-turn entries (keyword and lore-select activated, before or after the character definitions) where the book puts them; by default, with per-chat gating, they are placed a few messages from the end of the chat (install setting "Per-turn lore after the history", depth 4), so the start of the prompt stays the same from turn to turn and a local model can reuse it. Constant entries stay where the book puts them.
- **Good.** `{ "lorebooks": ["Sunken Ruins World"], "top_k": 6, "min_p": 0.7, "exclusive": true }`; raise `min_p` for a big book.
- **Bad.** A book that is not required.
- **Character eligibility.** Lore select respects each entry's SillyTavern character-name and tag include/exclude filters before rating or forcing it. Names match the drafted card's avatar filename without its extension; tags belong to that card. A change of drafted card or tags invalidates the forced-selection cache; a change during rating discards the result.
- **If wrong.** Lore select only reaches books SillyTavern scans, so a book not under requirements may never be in play (`lore-select-inactive`); `exclusive` with no book excludes nothing (`lore-select-exclusive-empty`).

<a id="lore-entries"></a>

## Lorebook entry features

Topic `lore-entries`.

Fields (on the wizard's `upsertLorebookEntry` step, written into SillyTavern's own entry fields): `keys` as `/pattern/flags`, `secondaryKeys`, `logic` (`and-any`, `not-all`, `not-any`, `and-all`), `outlet`, `triggers` (`wizard/provisioning.ts` `loreEntryShapeProblem`, `stHost/worldInfo.ts` `upsertWIEntry`).

- **What it does.** These are SillyTavern's own entry features; a story's books can use them and the runtime respects each one. A key written `/pattern/flags` is a regular expression and ignores the case and whole-word settings, so add `i` yourself. `secondaryKeys` narrow a keyword match: with `logic` `and-any` (the default) one of them must also appear, `and-all` every one, `not-any` none of them, `not-all` not every one. `outlet` places the text only where `{{outlet::name}}` is written (a card field, the preset, the Author's Note or another entry); higher `order` comes first there. `triggers` limit the generation types the entry fires on: `normal`, `continue`, `impersonate`, `swipe`, `regenerate`, `quiet`. On an update, a field the step leaves out keeps the entry's value, and a field it names empty (`secondaryKeys: []`, `outlet: ""`, `triggers: []`) clears it; `keys` are always the step's own list and an empty one keeps the entry's keywords. Lore select leaves an outlet entry in its outlet (late lore placement moves only entries placed before or after the character definitions), never asks the judge about an entry whose `triggers` leave out the reply being written (SillyTavern checks triggers before a forced entry, so the pick could never land), and counts a `not-any`/`not-all` entry as certain to fire only when nothing outside the chat is scanned with it (our scanned memory blocks and the Author's Note usually are, so such entries are rated like any other).
- **Good.** A tavern entry keyed `tavern` with `secondaryKeys: ["fight", "brawl"]`, `logic: "not-any"`, so its calm description stays out of a brawl; `/\bsilver (key|lock)s?\b/i` for one entry that covers every form; a map summary with `outlet: "map"` read by an Author's Note or card field that writes `{{outlet::map}}`; a recap entry with `triggers: ["quiet"]` for summaries only.
- **Bad.** A regex with an unescaped `/` inside it, which SillyTavern silently reads as plain text; secondary keys on an always-in-context entry, which skips every key check; an outlet nothing writes `{{outlet::name}}` for.
- **If wrong.** The wizard refuses these before you see them: a pattern key that would be read as plain text, a `logic` with no secondary keys, secondary keys on a constant entry or with no keyword, an outlet name holding `{` or `}`, an unknown trigger. An outlet with no `{{outlet::name}}` anywhere fires and lands nowhere; nothing warns about it, so check the prompt with SillyTavern's prompt inspector.
- **On the wizard's card.** Each entry step shows "Key matches these draft texts: …" (the checkpoint objectives, the briefing, and the descriptions and opening messages of the cards the wizard is proposing), or "No draft text contains any key". That line says where a key appears, not that the entry fires: real activation also depends on scan depth, what else is scanned, recursion and the budget. When the entry is one that may not fire even on a match, the card says why ("May not fire: only on quiet generations", "gated: on only from The Vault", "not-any depends on every text SillyTavern scans"). Key lint adds warnings, never refusals: a key under 3 characters; a key more than two entries in the book share; an `and-any` secondary key that repeats a primary key or shares its first 5 letters ("it narrows nothing"); sticky on an always-in-context entry (`copilot/lorePreview.ts`).

<a id="lore-content"></a>

## Lore content by kind

Topic `lore-content`.

Field: an entry's `content`, by what the entry describes (`copilot/prompts.ts` `LORE_CONTENT_RULE`).

- **What it does.** An entry is what the narrator knows when its key comes up, so it has to answer the questions a scene asks about that kind of thing. A place: the ways in and out, and how far it is from the places around it. An item: what it cannot do, and who wants it. A faction: how many they are and how far their reach goes. History: what happened, kept apart from what people say happened; the hidden truth stays out of shared lore (put it in a member's private knowledge or a gated entry). A concept (a power, a law, a ritual): its limits and its cost. Put a short "Current state" paragraph last, which the curator may patch as the story moves, and wrap the stable text above it in `{{// so:protect}}` … `{{// so:end}}` so the curator never rewrites it.
- **Good.** "The Old Lighthouse. Reached by the causeway at low tide, or by boat from the quay (half an hour's row). The keeper's stair is the only way to the lamp room. Current state: the lamp is dark."
- **Bad.** "The Old Lighthouse is mysterious and ancient." The narrator then invents the way in, the distance and who lives there, and invents them differently each time.
- **If wrong.** The narrator fills every unanswered basic with a guess, and two scenes contradict each other. The wizard writes entries by this rule.

<a id="scene-read"></a>

## Scene places and times

Topic `scene-read`.

Fields: `scene_read.locations`, `scene_read.times`, `scene_read.inject` (`schema.ts` `StorySceneRead`).

- **What it does.** The vocabulary the scene tracker picks from to say where and when the scene is. The judge only selects, so it needs a list. `inject: false` keeps the scene line out of the prompt.
- **Good.** `{ "locations": ["lowmarsh", "causeway", "ruined_gate"], "times": ["dawn", "day", "dusk", "night"] }`, with `player_labels` on a matching `location` enum.
- **Bad.** A free-text `location` quality and no list.
- **If wrong.** "The story can never say where the scene is, so nothing can key off a place." (`scene-read-location-empty`).

<a id="house-rules"></a>

## House rules

Topic `house-rules`.

Field: `house_rules[]`: at most 8 rules, each at most 240 characters, no duplicates (`schema.ts` `HOUSE_RULES_MAX`, `validate/storyOptions.ts` `readHouseRules`).

- **What it does.** Rules every reply is checked against by the continuity warden; a broken rule is named in the next reply's prompt. The check is on by default although it is below its measured floor (`judge.uses.houseRules`, `src/judge/settings.ts` `JUDGE_USES_OFF_BY_DEFAULT` is empty). It shares the warden's judge call under its own switch: the Continuity warden switch (`stagecraft.wardenEnabled`) covers the fact and lore check only.
- **Good.** `"{{user}}'s choices belong to {{user}}: show what the world does with an attempt, then stop."`; `"Magic is never used inside the city walls."`
- **Bad.** `"No magic in the city and keep replies short."`
- **If wrong.** The check asks one question per rule, so a rule with two demands is judged on whichever one the model reads (`house-rule-compound`). One rule, one demand; no "and" or `;` compounds.

The Judge settings also offer independent, default-on checks for answers to the player, low-cost world-pressure trends (18 of 20 replies), quiet stalls (3 of 4), tone drift (5 of 5, skipped at high tension), and repeated phrases. Trend hints use the warden's review or auto mode and only suggest developments; they never decide the player's action or write a quality. Repeated phrases always wait for review and require no model call. These checks run after a reply, with a four-second judge budget; a missing answer adds no hint. The quiet-stall check's comparison against extractor tension remains unmeasured.

Canon sentence verification runs before storing a regenerated story-so-far, with a three-second budget; unsupported answered sentences are removed, and missing answers preserve the usual synthesis. Author view's Memory controls can instead draft a checked story-so-far, inspect it, then accept or discard it. A draft stays out of play until accepted; changed sources refuse an old draft. The two canon actions have independent Judge switches.

With automatic illustrations enabled, Illustration-worthy replies checks whether an image is striking and happening now. It skips unsuitable cadence pictures and can notice an additional image, with a four-reply cooldown. Manual and checkpoint pictures keep their existing rules; a missing judge keeps the cadence rule. The check is off the text reply path and has a 2.5-second budget.

<a id="chapters"></a>

## Chapters

Topic `chapters`.

Fields: `chapters[]` (`id`, `title`, `player_title`, `kind`, `final`, `seal` with `open_threads`, `keep_tail`, `fold_messages`, `record_style`), `checkpoints[].chapter`, `memory.story_so_far` (`schema.ts` `Chapter`, `validate/chapters.ts`).

- **What it does.** Optional acts. Once one chapter is declared, every beat names one. When play leaves a chapter it is sealed into a written record, so later prompts carry the record instead of the whole transcript. `kind: "interlude"` never seals on its own; it seals with the next chapter. `final: true` marks the last chapter; the story ends when it reaches a beat with no exits there. `seal.open_threads` is `carry`, `close` or `decide`; `keep_tail` is how many messages stay verbatim after a fold (the fold is one block from the oldest message: it stops before a chapter with `fold_messages: false` or a gap, and an older chapter's tail folds once a later chapter seals, so Chat Completion never gets a hole in the history); `record_style` is `prose` or `chronicle`. `memory.story_so_far` (`block`, `macro`, `off`) is how the record reaches the prompt. Sealing is on by default, though its measurement floors have not run yet.
- **Good.** `[{ "id": "gate", "title": "Act I: The Gate", "player_title": "The Gate in the Water" }, { "id": "library", "title": "Act II: The Drowned Library", "player_title": "Beneath the Water", "final": true }]`.
- **Bad.** A `player_title` that names only the act's first place ("Lowmarsh" for an act that is about the ruins); a transition back into an earlier chapter.
- **If wrong.** A beat without a chapter, or naming an unknown one, stops the story loading (`chapter-missing`, `chapter-unknown`). An unreachable chapter is never written up (`chapter-unreachable`); a non-final chapter with no way out is never closed (`chapter-no-exit`); going back reopens a closed record (`chapter-reentry`); a beat with no way on outside a final chapter means the last chapter is never written up (`story-dead-end`).

<a id="consequences"></a>

## Consequences recap

Topic `consequences`.

Fields: `recap` and `recap_when` on `transitions[]`, `quests[]` (`recap: {done?, failed?}`) and `milestones[]`; `qualities[].player_action` (`schema.ts` `Transition`, `RecapText`, `Quality`; `gameSchema.ts` `Quest`, `Milestone`; `validate/recap.ts`).

- **What it does.** At a chapter's end the chapter title card lists what changed in the chapter that ended, and the Overview and `/story recap` list what changed in this chapter (a story without chapters lists the last 20 turns, labelled recent). At most five lines, authored first. Three kinds of line, strictest first: your own `recap` line, shown only when its effect is one the player can see (a reached place with a `player_name`, a visible quest, an earned milestone; `recap_when` narrows it further, read when the effect happens); a "because you" line, only when the player's own committed line decided the effect; otherwise a neutral line in the Journal's words ("Reached The Gatehouse", "Quest complete: …", "Milestone: …", a public check, a public agenda step). The section is titled "Because of you" only when an authored or because-you line is in it, else "What changed". No model writes any of it.
- **`recap`.** A line, or `{text, because}`. `text` is shown whenever the effect is visible. `because` is shown instead only when the player's committed line decided the effect: a single-condition gate (or the last condition of an `all`) on a quality with `commit_evidence`, false the turn before, written by that player line and not overwritten, with no other way out open at the same turn. An `any` gate, a gate that already held, two conditions turning together, an NPC's or a code write never earn it, so most effects read neutral; that is by design. On a quest, `recap` is `{done, failed}`.
- **`player_action`.** On an enum or bool quality with `commit_evidence`, a map from value to an action clause ("took the posting"). When the evidence holds and there is no authored `because`, the line reads "Reached The Gatehouse, because you took the posting." It is not `player_labels`: a label names a state, a player action says what the player did. A value without a commit pattern cannot carry one.
- **Good.** `{"from": "board", "to": "gate", "gate": {"q": "posting", "op": "==", "v": "taken"}, "priority": 1, "recap": {"text": "The garrison opened its gates.", "because": "Because you took the posting, the garrison opened its gates."}}` with `"player_action": {"taken": "took the posting"}` on `posting`.
- **Bad.** A recap line that names a place the player has not reached or a quest still hidden: the line is dropped (and the neutral line with it if that also names it). A `because` written as plain `text`: it would be shown even when an NPC caused the change.
- **If wrong.** `recap_when` without `recap`, a `player_action` on a value with no `commit_evidence`, or a line over 240 characters stops the story loading.

<a id="patterns"></a>

## Story patterns (callbacks)

Topic `patterns`.

Fields: `patterns[]` (`id`, `steps` with `kind`, `id`, `to`, `where`; `unless` with `between`; `within`, `repeat`, `label.text`, `hint`, `pending`) (`engine/patternSchema.ts`, `validate/patterns.ts`, `runtime/patterns.ts`, `runtime/patternsPort.ts`).

- **What it does.** A pattern notices an order of things the player could see happen, and lets you call it back. Each step is one visible event: a reached checkpoint (`kind: "transition"`, attributes `to`, `from`, `chapter`), a quest that moved (`kind: "quest"`, `id`, `to` = offered, active, done or failed, `giver`), an earned milestone (`kind: "milestone"`, `id`) or a public check (`kind: "check"`, `id`, `outcome` = success, failure, miss, weak or strong, `quality`). `id` and `to` are shorthands for those attributes (on a check `to` is the outcome); `where` names any of them. A value written `"?name"` binds on its first step and must match on later ones ("the same giver"); a pattern uses at most two. At most 3 steps, matched in code at each turn in the order the story recorded them, never by a model; within one turn the order is the order the recap lists them (checkpoint, quests, milestones, checks), not the order of the prose. `unless` rows (`between: [i, j]`, steps counted from 1) cancel a match when such an event happens after step i and before step j. `within` limits the turns from the first step to the last (that many turns still match). `repeat: "once"` (the default) completes once per chat, even after an edit or after you remove and re-add it; `"each"` completes again, never reusing an event.
- **What the player sees.** When a pattern completes, `label.text` is one line in What changed (an authored line, never "because you"), `hint` goes to the narrator for 3 turns as something already true of the party, to show through bodies, mood and the world's response (never as a cause), and `pending` is the line other features read while exactly one step is left. Every one of them is withheld whole, not edited, when it names a place, quest or person the player has not met, or restates a secret the story keeps from the resting view; it is checked again each time it is shown. A swipe or edit takes the completion back with the turn. Author view lists live partial matches, cancelled and expired ones, completions and anything withheld (Author › Memory › Patterns).
- **Good.** `{ "id": "two-favours", "steps": [{ "kind": "quest", "to": "done", "where": { "giver": "?who" } }, { "kind": "quest", "to": "done", "where": { "giver": "?who" } }], "label": { "text": "Two favours done for the same patron." }, "pending": "One more favour for a familiar patron would make two." }`; `{ "id": "second-try", "steps": [{ "kind": "check", "id": "climb", "to": "failure" }, { "kind": "check", "id": "climb", "to": "success" }], "within": 10, "hint": "The cliff that beat them once has now been climbed." }`.
- **Bad.** A label that explains why ("because you were kind, …"): a pattern sees order, not cause (`pattern-label-claims-cause`). A label naming someone the player meets later (`pattern-label-names-unknown-entity`). A step on a checkpoint no path reaches, or a quest move the quest can never make (`pattern-never-completes`). A secret milestone, a hidden check or a living (`liv_`) checkpoint: refused, a pattern reads only what the player can see.
- **If wrong.** An unknown kind, attribute, id or value, more than 3 steps or 2 variables, an `unless` naming a variable no earlier step binds, `within` outside 1 to 200, a text over 240 characters, or a pattern with no label, hint or pending line stops the story loading.

<a id="outcome"></a>

## Outcome a next story can carry

Topic `outcome`.

Fields: `outcome[]` (`key`, `heritage_text`) (`engine/carrySchema.ts`, `validate/carry.ts`, `engine/carry.ts`).

- **What it does.** Names up to 12 keys a sequel, or a replay of this same story, may carry from a run that finished (its `final` chapter sealed). A key is an authored quality, a quest's `quest_<id>_closed` or a faction's standing `rep_<id>`. Only a value the player saw at the end carries: the `heritage_text` line for that value, else the quality's `player_labels` word, else its `display` label with the value; a quest only while it was visible (its title with the done or failed word); a faction only while it was visible (its band word, never the number). A key whose ending value was not shown to the player does not carry, and the next story keeps its own start for it. The epilogue written at the final seal is told from these same lines (HOW IT ENDED), never from the rest of the blackboard; a story without `outcome` gives the epilogue no end state at all.
- **Finished stories.** Any run that ends (its `final` chapter sealed), with or without `outcome`, is listed under Continue › Finished stories in the settings panel, newest first and at most 20, each only after its saved state is read and checked (a pinned copy that parses and a `final` chapter record): the story title, the final chapter's player title and the story's non-secret `milestones` its ending had earned, filtered through that run's held secrets. No value, epilogue or secret milestone is shown, and nothing is read until the player opens the list.
- **Good.** `{ "outcome": [{ "key": "village_fate", "heritage_text": { "saved": "You saved the village of Lowmarsh.", "flooded": "Lowmarsh flooded while you watched." } }, { "key": "quest_ledger_closed" }, { "key": "rep_guild" }] }`.
- **Bad.** A code key such as `message_count`, a `rep_<id>_move_*` record, `tension` or a `liv_` key (refused: "nothing of it can carry into a next story"); a `heritage_text` key that is not a value the quality can take (refused: the line would never show); a line over 240 characters (refused).
- **If wrong.** A sequel that maps a key missing from `outcome` is refused at import when this story is in the library, and otherwise its finished runs are simply not offered.

<a id="carry-from"></a>

## Carry from a finished run

Topic `carry-from`.

Fields: `carry_from.story`, `carry_from.mode`, `carry_from.map` (`from`, `to`, `as`, `known_by`), `carry_from.replay_map`, `carry_from.previously`, `carry_from.default` (`engine/carrySchema.ts`, `validate/carry.ts`, `runtime/carryCandidate.ts`, `runtime/carryUnit.ts`).

- **What it does.** Declares that this story can start from how a finished run of another story ended (`mode: "sequel"`, `story` its id) or of this same story (`mode: "replay"`, `story` this story's own id). In a new group chat the start pane lists the player's finished runs of that story, newest first, at most 20, and shows a run only after reading its saved state: it ended, it played that story, and every `from` key is there and fits. Picking one pins a copy of what carries in this chat (later edits, swipes or deletion of the other chat change nothing) and starts the story with it. Each `map` entry takes an `outcome` key (`from`) into a key of this story (`to`): `as: "heritage"` lands in a `heritage_` quality, which you declare with `source: "code"` and which only the carry writes (gates may read it; it is the player's heritage, shown on a card, never in-world progress); `as: "state"` lands in an ordinary extractor quality, as if the story had started with it. `known_by` names the roster members who know the carried value (a private line "From an earlier story, you know: …"), `"all"` or `"none"`; the default is nobody, because the player having seen something does not mean every character in the next story knows it. `previously` (default true) adds a short "Previously…" note to the start pane and to the narrator's prompt, composed from what the player saw (the ending chapter's title, the heritage lines and the chapter records' short lines, a held secret left out), at most about 350 tokens, kept until the first chapter seal, 12 turns or the player's Dismiss, whichever is first, and never on quiet or impersonate generations. `default: "snapshot"` lets the player start fresh instead; `"require"` makes a run necessary: the start pane offers no "Start fresh". Restart keeps the pinned copy and checks it again against the restarted story; a value that no longer fits is dropped and written in the journal.
- **Replay.** A replay carries `heritage` values only, so a carried "done" never skips the story being replayed. `replay_map` lists keys a replay may carry `as: "state"`; a key any transition, quest or milestone gate reads is refused there.
- **Good.** `{ "carry_from": { "story": "lowmarsh", "mode": "sequel", "map": [{ "from": "village_fate", "to": "heritage_lowmarsh", "as": "heritage", "known_by": ["mara"] }, { "from": "rep_guild", "to": "guild_trust", "as": "state" }], "default": "snapshot" } }` with `{ "key": "heritage_lowmarsh", "type": "enum", "values": ["saved", "flooded"], "source": "code", "rubric": "How Lowmarsh ended in the earlier story" }`.
- **Bad.** `as: "heritage"` into a key without the `heritage_` prefix; `as: "state"` into a code, `heritage_`, `rep_*` or character-life key; a `heritage_` quality that is not `source: "code"`, that nothing carries into, or that a `state_snapshot` or reward writes; `mode: "replay"` naming another story, or `"sequel"` naming this one; a `known_by` id outside the roster; a `to` that does not declare every value the `from` key can take (each refused).
- **If wrong.** A run that does not carry what the map needs is not offered (no error to the player); at import, with the earlier story in the library, a mismatch refuses the save and names the key.
